sections.h2: Where is Murray, Utah, and which cities does it touch?
sections.html:
Murray sits in the core of the Salt Lake Valley on the Wasatch Front, bordered by Taylorsville, Holladay, South Salt Lake, Millcreek and West Jordan. The Jordan River forms its western edge, and Big and Little Cottonwood Creeks join the river inside the city limits.

The city is at about 4,301 feet and covers 12.32 square miles by Census measure. It had 50,637 residents in 2020, up from 46,746 in 2010.

sections.h2: How did Murray grow from a smelter town into a healthcare hub?
sections.html:
Murray was settled in 1848, named for Territorial Governor Eli Houston Murray, and incorporated as a third class city on January 3, 1903. The post office had been renamed from South Cottonwood to Murray in 1883.

Smelting drove the early economy. The first smelter went up around 1870, and ASARCO formed in 1899 and closed its lead smelter in 1949. The stacks were imploded in 2000, and Intermountain Healthcare bought the site. Intermountain Medical Center, which replaced Cottonwood Hospital in 2007, is a major employer in the city.

Retail came next. Fashion Place Mall opened in the 1970s, and State Street became a corridor of car dealerships. The city has also drawn several private college campuses, including University of Phoenix, Stevens-Henager College and Eagle Gate College, according to Wikipedia.

sections.h2: Why does Murray run so many of its own utilities?
sections.html:
Murray operates its own police, fire, power, water, sewer, library and parks departments. The city's utility billing page says it provides power, water, sewer, garbage and stormwater service in many areas, while other providers serve properties where the city has no infrastructure.

Murray City Power is a publicly owned electric utility created in 1913. It serves about 18,000 customers, 82 percent residential and 18 percent commercial and industrial, with 47 employees.

  • Call the utility billing office at (801) 264-2626 to ask how a final reading and a transfer of service work at your address.
  • The office is at 10 East 4800 South, Suite 160. Pay only through the city's own website, since the page warns that look-alike sites solicit Murray customers.
  • Because the provider depends on the address, ask whether your water and sewer come from the city or another provider before you list.

sections.h2: What do Murray TRAX, FrontRunner and the interstates mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Murray has three light rail stations, a commuter rail connection and two interstates, so a seller has real transit access to point to. The three TRAX stations are Murray North, Murray Central and Fashion Place West, on the Blue and Red lines.

FrontRunner commuter rail opened in December 2012, and Murray Central is the only station outside Salt Lake City where FrontRunner and TRAX connect. Interstate 15 and Interstate 215 both pass through the city.

The Census Bureau puts mean travel time to work at 20.7 minutes. Distance to a station is a fair thing to mention in any Murray listing.

sections.h2: Which schools and neighborhoods define Murray?
sections.html:
Murray has its own school district, created January 1, 1906, with ten schools and over 6,000 students. Murray High School, Hillcrest Junior High, Riverview Junior High and seven elementaries (Grant, Horizon, Liberty, Longview, McMillan, Parkside and Viewmont) make up the district.

Some Murray addresses are in a different district. Granite School District runs Cottonwood High School and Woodstock Elementary inside Murray, so the school an address belongs to depends on the street.

  • Bergertown, south of 4800 South along Little Cottonwood Creek, began as a Swiss immigrant enclave.
  • The Murray Downtown Historic District runs along State Street.
  • Murray City Park covers 22 acres and has a baseball stadium and an amphitheatre.
  • The Jordan River Parkway trail follows the western edge, and Wheeler Historic Farm shows farm life from 1890 to 1920.

sections.h2: What rules apply to Murray rental houses and accessory units?
sections.html:
Murray treats residential rentals as a business, so an owner needs a current Murray business license for them. One license covers all rentals owned by the same legal entity, and a property manager does not replace the owner's license.

Licenses cannot be transferred between owners or addresses, so a buyer who keeps your tenants must apply for their own. Operating without a license, or after one lapses, carries a penalty of 100 percent of the past-due fees under City Code 5.04.280. Re-application notices go out on the first of the month the license expires, and postmarks do not count as proof of timely receipt.

Accessory dwelling units are limited to one per lot, and the owner must live in the main house or the unit. Detached units need a lot of at least 10,000 square feet, a height of 20 feet or less and a single story, and cannot sit in the front yard. The city prohibits renting an ADU for stays shorter than 30 days. An affidavit on occupancy and short-term rental terms must be recorded by the Salt Lake County Recorder before the application is accepted, so the document is on record with the county.

sections.h2: What should a Murray seller know about the ground and the creeks?
sections.html:
Murray sits on the Wasatch Front, where the Wasatch Fault and soft lake sediments shape the building risk for the whole valley. Wikipedia's fault entry says many Wasatch Front areas sit on soft Lake Bonneville sediments, which raises liquefaction risk, and that the Salt Lake City segment last broke 1,200 to 1,300 years ago.

The same entry gives a 57 percent chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years. For a Murray seller, the practical point is to have a plan for what a buyer's inspector will flag: chimney bracing, a strapped water heater and any foundation cracking. Big and Little Cottonwood Creeks both run through the city on their way to the Jordan River, so ask the county for flood zone information on a lot near either creek.

sections.h2: How do Murray property taxes and recording work?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County values and bills Murray property, and the county's published calendar governs every date a seller needs.

  • All property is valued as it stood on January 1.
  • Valuation notices are mailed in July and August, and the Board of Equalization window runs 45 days from the original mailing.
  • Real property tax notices are mailed by November 1.
  • November 30 is the last day to pay without penalty, and December 1 is when unpaid taxes become delinquent.

Before a deed is recorded, the county's 2024 recording requirements call for white 8.5 by 11 inch paper, a legible caption on the first page, the grantee's name and mailing address, and a legal description. The grantor's name must match across the title, the document, the notary acknowledgment and the signature. The county's schedule listed a flat $40 recording fee at that time, so confirm the current amount before you sign.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Murray seller?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Murray follows the usual closing steps through a title company but without a buyer's lender. We look at the house as it is, make an offer, and the title company handles signing and recording at the county.

Sellers in Murray often call us about inherited homes, rentals with tenants, and houses that need work. If the offer does not fit, you can decline it.

faqs.q: What school district is Murray, Utah in?
faqs.a: Most of Murray is in Murray City School District, which has ten schools. Granite School District runs Cottonwood High School and Woodstock Elementary inside the city, so check the district for a specific address.

Murray City Power, a municipal utility created in 1913, serves about 18,000 customers in the city. Water, sewer and garbage service also come from the city in many areas, and other providers serve the rest.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a Murray house?
faqs.a: Yes. Murray treats residential rentals as a business, and one license covers all rentals owned by the same legal entity. The license cannot be transferred to a buyer.

faqs.q: Can I rent an accessory dwelling unit short term in Murray?
faqs.a: No. Murray prohibits collecting rent for guest stays shorter than 30 days in an ADU, and the owner must live on the property.

faqs.q: When are Murray property taxes due?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County lists November 30 as the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1.
